summary: Chelan County, WA cupola lookout built 1919 on Stormy Mountain; a Sept 1930 fire destroyed the station, an L-4 cab followed, and it was removed or destroyed in 1955.

facts.design: Cupola cabin (1919), then a gable-roofed L-4 cab (1930)
facts.status_note: L-4 cab removed or destroyed in 1955; no source describes what remains on the summit today

access.note: The hiking guide describes a gravel-road approach and a 1.2-mile hike to the summit and mentions no closure. No Forest Service statement was read.

visit.trail_note: Guide: 1.2 miles and 1,100 ft of gain; gravel roads, some clearance best, good tires. Check conditions before going.

resolved_conflicts.field: fate of the L-4 cab in 1930 and the fire
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register, firelookout.com and the guide say an L-4 cab replaced the cupola in 1930. A Wenatchee Daily World item reports that the station was destroyed by fire in September 1930. A Leavenworth Echo item says replacing it would cost at least $1,200, with funds doubtful before 1931. The guide suggests the 1930 style change may date the fire instead, citing a 1984 book. The sources do not settle which came first.
The register says the cab was removed in 1955. firelookout.com and the guide say it was destroyed that year. The story reports both words.

A Wenatchee Daily World item says Richardson left for his homestead the day before the fire. A later Leavenworth Echo item gives September 10 as the date he had to leave his station. The story does not give a departure date.

notes_for_editor: Brief status 'gone' confirmed. No source describes what remains on the summit now; the guide has a photo labelled 2018 with no description, so nothing is said about remains. Access is marked public from the hiking guide, which mentions no closure; no Forest Service statement was read. Staffing dates come from newspapers quoted on the Forest Lookouts page and from firelookout.com. A second-hand, undated anecdote about Richardson on the guide page is not used. The 1930 fire and L-4 timeline needs a primary check (Wenatchee newspaper or Forest Service report) before publication.
